contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, DAG, the envelope schema
Records: envelope, append-only table, entities, epoch, idempotency, compare-and-swap, migrations, stream, apply
Principals, seat users and the effects outbox
Leases: table, fencing, heartbeats, attempts, slots
Tickets: tickets, claims, ticket sets, id mint
Service tables: forge, backups, ticks, health, code table, registry, plans

pointers.shared: The envelope as JSON Schema 2020-12; every node schema should $ref it
The cross-node shapes: commit request and reply, lease row, effect row, cursor, store epoch
Principals and peer credentials behind the principals and seat_users tables
N-01 owns the store, the migrations of the core tables and the id form
N-02 owns leases, the fencing token counter and heartbeats
N-45 owns retention and the cleanup registry

purpose.s: One store, no broker (principles.xml#one-store): SQLite in WAL mode at STATE/store/coq.db, opened by the Go service alone, served over one gRPC unix socket; every record of every node is a row here and nothing lives on a branch, in a file tree or in a second database.
The node that owns a table owns its forward-only migration; a node that needs a column on another node's table cuts a ticket against that node's volume.
This volume names the tables and rules; the owning node volume carries the mechanism and the schema beside it.

store-rule.title: The record envelope every kind carries
store-rule.statement: Fields (the one envelope, shared/state-store.schema.json#/$defs/envelope): required id (string, form YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-CODE-xxxxx: UTC stamp, the code, five lowercase alphanumerics; unique per writer), kind (dotted lowercase), code (an integer in the live code table) and node (N-xx that wrote it; checked against the caller, shared/authority.xml#role-derivation); optional on input at (UTC 2006-01-02T15:04:05Z, assigned by N-01 at commit when absent), by (set by N-01 from the authenticated caller), attempt (0..3 where one applies; 0 means none), ticket (WO-id or CR-id), recovery_of (on a 2xx record, the id of the alerting record it resolves; nodes/N-41/spec.xml), note (max 240) and schema_version (when present, 2.0.0); set by N-01 at commit, never trusted on input: seq, epoch (contracts.xml#epoch-cursor) and hash (canonical JSON by RFC 8785 of the body). A committed record carries seq, at and epoch (committed_envelope), which is what N-07 and every reader requires.

Not envelope fields: the commit request (contracts.xml#batch, contracts.schema.json#/$defs/commit_request) carries the operation_key (contracts.xml#operation-keys; required on every Commit), the lease it acts under as {key, token} (contracts.xml#fencing), preconditions, entity writes, owner-registered statements and outbox effects. Lease state lives only in the leases table (contracts.xml#lease-machine); there is no lease:KEY entity. A lease body names its fencing token token and its key key (ticket:phase:attempt or a system key, contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_key). The token is an integer from counter:lease_token: the string form t-000184 and a lease: prefix on a record field were rejected because N-01 (fencing), N-02 (lease_body) and N-07 (dispatch) carry an integer token and an unprefixed key.

Ruling on the id form: N-01 owns the records table and today's event writers already mint the UTC-stamp form (events/schema/event.schema.json), so the book keeps it; the r-prefixed form some G4 and G7 schemas repeat is rejected with reason (rejected-with-reason.xml#envelope-id-form) and those schemas $ref state-store.schema.json#/$defs/envelope by their own ticket.
store-rule.source: N-01 spec.xml#input; events/schema/event.schema.json; nodes/N-02/record.schema.json#/$defs/lease_granted (the example validates against it, bin/check-examples.py, check C22: a seat lease as GrantDispatch leaves it, reserved with the start grace, holder the dispatch id); G5 schemas embed it by allOf; N-43 record.schema.json#/$defs/envelope.

store-table.name: records
store-table.purpose: Every record of every kind; the only log; seq strictly increasing and never reused, not gapless (contracts.xml#epoch-cursor); a row is never updated; N-45 retention deletes rows of expired classes and advances store:epoch min_retained_seq in the same Commit.
store-table.rule: Indexes: (kind, seq), (ticket, seq), (code, seq); the query "newest record of kind K for key X with code C" is one index read.

A record whose code is not in the live code table is 400 with the live hash in the reason; a kind the authenticated principal may not write is 403 record.refused (kind_not_permitted, shared/authority.xml#role-derivation); a duplicate id is 409 record.conflict reason id.

Every write is one Store.Commit (contracts.xml#batch): its records, entity writes, statements and effects commit all or none under one operation key (N-51 verdict plus freeze flip, N-18 set admission plus id mint, GrantDispatch).

store-table.name: entities
store-table.purpose: Current state by key (counters, snapshots, health, ticks, page state, run:RUN_ID, kill:RUN_ID, store:epoch); every write is compare-and-swap on version inside a Commit; an entity-only kind appends no record unless its state changes (contracts.xml#entity-only), every other entity write rides with the record that explains it.
store-table.rule: version grows by one per write; updated_seq is the seq of the record that last wrote it (unchanged by an entity-only write); expected 0 inserts. counter:lease_token's version is the last issued token (contracts.xml#dispatch).

store-rule.title: Entity store:epoch
store-rule.statement: Entity store:epoch (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/store_epoch): epoch, started_at, cause (created, restored, migrated), min_retained_seq. Created at epoch 1 with the store; bumped only by a restore (contracts.xml#restore); min_retained_seq advanced by N-45 retention. Every record, Tail frame and cursor carries the epoch (contracts.xml#epoch-cursor).

store-table.name: idempotency
store-table.purpose: One row per committed operation key (contracts.xml#operation-keys): the same key with the same request hash replays the stored reply with 200 reason replayed and writes nothing; the same key with a different request hash is 409 idempotency_mismatch before any write or effect.
store-table.column: operation key, contracts.schema.json#/$defs/operation_key; its node segment equals the authenticated caller's node
the kind of the first record, or entity when the Commit wrote entities only
sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical commit request with every record's id, at, seq and hash removed
the first seq the Commit appended
the commit_reply
store-table.rule: The key forms in use are the op-key rows of contracts.xml#operation-keys and nowhere else; one effect, one key.
store-table.retention: Kept as long as the records it names; deleted with them by N-45.

store-rule.title: Idempotent commits
store-rule.statement: Every automated step commits under its operation key; a retry of the step replays the first reply (200) and never creates a second record or effect; a step whose outcome is unknown re-runs by its key (failure-cases.xml#unknown-outcome), and an external effect is looked up by its op_id before any resend (contracts.xml#outbox).

store-rule.title: Compare-and-swap
store-rule.statement: An entity write carries expected_version; a miss is 409 reason version with the current version in the reply and the writer re-reads; expected 0 inserts; used by counter:lease_token, merge.hold.lifted, forge:snapshot, backup:latest, tick:*, health:service, store:epoch, run:*, kill:*, break-glass.token, alert.ack, the tier pointer, page.state, ack, plan.step and plan.side. Node-owned table rows (leases, tickets, claims, flags, effects) change only through owner-registered statements (contracts.xml#statements), each guarded by the row's version.

store-rule.title: Forward-only migrations
store-rule.statement: Table migrations(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name, node, applied_at); applied in order at open inside one transaction each; never a down migration; the node owning a table owns its migration file under scheduler/internal/store/migrations/ and its test; a migration that fails leaves the store closed (store.corrupt 500) rather than half-applied.

store-rule.title: The record.committed stream
store-rule.statement: Store.Tail(class, filter, cursor) streams committed records in seq order over gRPC with the cursor {epoch, seq} (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/cursor); a cursor of another epoch, below min_retained_seq or above the high-water seq is answered cursor.expired and the client takes Store.Snapshot, one read transaction returning the state and its seq, before tailing again (contracts.xml#epoch-cursor, principles.xml#level-triggered). Entity-only kinds arrive as coalesced entity frames. Slow consumers are N-31's: one drop rule, push.max_pending and push.send_timeout_s; nothing is lost because the log is the truth.

store-rule.title: Apply rules by kind
store-rule.statement: Compare-and-swap upsert by version for page.state, ack, plan.step and plan.side; append-only for ledger.row, reply and owner.message, applied idempotently by record id; page.state is entity-only (contracts.xml#entity-only), the others are records the stream carries.

store-rule.title: The code table
store-rule.statement: Table code_table(hash UNIQUE, main_sha, loaded_at, version, body JSON): the status code map loaded by N-43 from shared/status-codes.xml at the merge sha; N-01 reads the newest row to validate every put; a failed load keeps the previous row and writes code.table 400 with the live hash.

store-table.name: principals
store-table.purpose: Who a peer is: the store socket (/run/coq/store.sock 0660, group coq-store) reads SO_PEERCRED and maps the uid here; the server derives role, the nodes the caller may act as and its permitted kinds; an unknown uid is 403 unknown_principal (shared/authority.xml#principals, #peer-credentials). Written at install by the owner CLI from scheduler/config/principals.json (planned) and changed only by a ruling.
store-table.column: owner, coq-svc, coq-launch, coq-seat-01 to coq-seat-16
owner, service, launcher or seat (contracts.schema.json#/$defs/principal_role)
node ids whose operation keys it may use
store-table.rule: A seat principal has no socket access; a row with role seat exists so a forged peer is refused by name, never by absence.

store-table.name: seat_users
store-table.purpose: Which pool user runs which run, one run at a time, scrubbed between runs (shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation); written by statement seat_users.bind in the run.start Commit.
store-table.rule: A pool user is bound only when scrubbed_at is later than its last run's end; bind and scrub are compare-and-swap on version.

store-table.name: effects
store-table.purpose: The outbox (contracts.xml#outbox; row contracts.schema.json#/$defs/effect_row): one row per external effect, inserted with state intent in the Commit of the record that decides it; advanced by statement effects.advance.
store-table.column: intent, sent, accepted, unknown, done, failed
store-table.rule: Index (state, provider); a worker picks rows in intent or unknown; done only after the provider read-back.
store-table.retention: done and failed rows 30 days, with their records.

store-table.name: leases
store-table.purpose: The only lease state (no lease:KEY entity): one row per key, the state machine of contracts.xml#lease-machine, row shape contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_row.
store-table.column: contracts.schema.json#/$defs/lease_key: ticket:phase:attempt for a seat-class lease (CR-<request id>:spec:attempt for a cut request); a system key otherwise (node:N-07:leader, merge.lock, watcher/<page>, cleanup:ENTRY, workspace:TICKET, seat:RUN, tier:NAME, backup:SNAPSHOT, publish:drive, unlanded:run, cutover:run, exittest:DAY)
seat, work or maintenance
reserved, running, released, expired, revoked
never empty: the dispatch id for a seat lease, node and job otherwise
store-table.rule: Every change is a statement of contracts.xml#statements (leases.grant, acquire, start, renew, release, sweep, revoke) whose guards and effects are the rows of contracts.xml#lease-machine; the token comes from counter:lease_token and only grows; generation bumps only on grant; timings are the keys of contracts.xml#timing (lease.ttl_seconds, start.grace_seconds, merge.lock_seconds, lease.leader_ttl_seconds).
A script may ask whether a path is held (lease list --path) before it deletes anything (N-45).

store-rule.title: Fencing tokens
store-rule.statement: contracts.xml#fencing: a write under a lease is current only when the row for its key is reserved or running, the token matches and expires_at has not passed at commit; else 412 stale_token or lease_not_current (record.stale); the one exception is contracts.xml#terminal-report. N-39 shows the token beside the last records; a stale writer exits.

store-table.name: heartbeats
store-table.purpose: Latest heartbeat per run (upsert with monotonic seq; entity-only, contracts.xml#entity-only: no record per beat); N-12 reads it for the stall bound; N-39 shows the age.
store-table.rule: A heartbeat is fenced like any write (contracts.xml#fencing, 412); adopted is true after a launcher restart re-attached to the run's unit coq-seat-RUN_ID (contracts.xml#run-states). Two launchers on one run cannot exist: the unit name is unique and run:RUN_ID moves by compare-and-swap.

store-table.name: attempts
store-table.purpose: One row per charged attempt of a ticket phase with its backoff and outcome; dead after 3; who charges is contracts.xml#retry-owner.
store-table.rule: Unique on (ticket, phase, n); backoff min(10 s x 2^(n-1), 300 s); row 4 never exists.

store-table.name: slots
store-table.purpose: Workspace slots 1..workspace_slots; compare-and-swap from null to holder; reclaimed by expiry plus seat.result.

store-table.name: tickets
store-table.purpose: The whole ticket; status is contracts.schema.json#/$defs/ticket_status and phase is its own column.
store-table.column: rebuild or product
commands with expected and observed_exit_on_main

set by N-03 when it admits the ticket set cut from N-10's fix-for-hold ticket.request (rejected_id plus hold_id); N-09 reads it for the hold exception; a second fix ticket naming a hold is refused until the first is verified or dead
with source_sha when files come from feat/go-scheduler-design-one-xml-spec-per-domain-unde (small cut)
store-table.rule: Transitions: only the rows of contracts.xml#ticket-transitions, through statement tickets.transition; any other pair, owner or a stale from status is refused 412 precondition with ticket.transition_refused. cancelled carries reason and ruling id.
Queries: by status at a sha; children of an epic by status; by kind and by over an at range.

store-table.name: claims
store-table.purpose: The one claim authority (contracts.xml#claims): taken in the Commit of a transition whose claims attribute is acquire, released in the Commit of one whose attribute is release; the N-14 file_claims table of book 1.0.0 is deleted.
store-table.column: the literal part before the first glob metacharacter
store-table.rule: Overlap is two-way prefix containment against live claims of other tickets, checked inside the Commit; own claims excluded; a non-unique partial index on prefix where released_at is null; the only update is released_at from null, by statement claims.release.
A second live ticket on tools/map/registry/** or on one screen volume overlaps by prefix and is refused (N-37).

store-table.name: ticket_sets
store-table.purpose: ticket-set.draft and ticket-set.accepted by set_id with anchor, repo_sha, attempt and verdict_ref.

store-table.name: id_mint
store-table.purpose: Reserved ticket ids, unique on (set_id, key) and on id, so a crashed mint resumes with the same ids.

store-table.name: flags
store-table.purpose: The three flags: build-mode, hold, freeze; each with state, scope, expiry, the card and ruling that set it. N-44 is the only writer of every row (statement flags.set); N-29 rulings and N-42 Controls actions reach N-44 as ruling effects and never write a flag themselves.
store-table.column: rebuild or all

store-rule.title: The hold flag
store-rule.statement: flag:hold (a row of flags) is set and cleared only by N-44, from an owner ruling (N-29) or a Controls action (N-42) that names it, or by a restore (contracts.xml#restore); N-03, N-07 and N-09 read it inside the Commit that would dispatch or merge; GrantDispatch and work-class leases are refused 423 hold while maintenance leases, ticks, health, backups, the poll and the push transport run (contracts.xml#lease-machine).

store-rule.title: Build mode state
store-rule.statement: Flags row build-mode (record kind build-mode.state): state on or off, scope, expires_at, ruling_id, version; written by N-44, read by N-07 in the GrantDispatch Commit and copied into the dispatch as contracts.schema.json#/$defs/build_mode with its version; cleared by N-44 at expiry (flags.build_mode.max_duration) with one card when rebuild tickets are still open.

store-table.name: forge_history
store-table.purpose: Entity forge:snapshot (main_sha, previous_main_sha, changed_paths, main_gate, prs[] with head sha, head repository, base ref, mergeability, changed files and the coq/gate status: state, description, target_url, updated_at; hash, polled_at, stale, failed_since, etags) is written every poll by compare-and-swap; this table is appended on hash change.
store-table.retention: forge.keep_days 30; cleanup-forge.sh; the live entity is never touched.

store-table.name: backups
store-table.purpose: One row per snapshot under STATE/backup/store/ (nodes/N-05/spec.xml); entities backup:latest (compare-and-swap) and backup:running (expected absent). The snapshot is taken on a reader connection in one read transaction, so the writer is never blocked.
store-table.column: tick, daily, monthly, manual
the verifier checks max(seq) equals it
the verifier checks count(*) equals it (seq is not gapless)
the verifier checks min(seq) is at or above it
store-table.retention: backup.retention (tick 48 h, daily 30 d, monthly 12 months, manual until the owner's cleanup card); the newest verified backup is never deleted; an off-host copy older than backup.rpo_offhost_hours raises one card.

store-rule.title: Ticks
store-rule.statement: Entities tick:SUBKIND (n, at, interval_seconds, duration_ms, class for backup) written by compare-and-swap once per tick (scheduler, poll, backup, stall, health, hourly, daily); entity-only (contracts.xml#entity-only), so a tick writes no record; the tick minute keys a counters window; a skipped tick is tick.missed once per subkind and counters.failed for the stats screen.

store-rule.title: Health
store-rule.statement: Entity health:service (status, reasons[], counters, version, config_hash, at; includes the Jenkins GET /api/json probe with a 10 s timeout, unknown when missing), entity-only with a record only on a status transition, and table health_history(at, status, reasons JSON) appended on transition; pruned by cleanup-logs.sh --health.

store-rule.title: The record kinds registry
store-rule.statement: Every record kind with its code set, class (record, line-op, owner-surface, plan, screen), writer node, schema path and, where the owning volume says so, the entity-only mark (contracts.xml#entity-only); loaded by N-43 with the code table; a record of an unregistered kind is 400 and a kind under a code not listed for it is 400.

The registry is generated: shared/record-kinds.xml, written by rebuild/design/bin/make-kinds.py from the status-codes section of every node volume, so the node that emits a kind is the only place it is declared (check.sh C15 refuses a stale file; C18 refuses a kind whose code row in status-codes.xml does not name it). What broke (gap review R-03, 2026-10-14): the hand list that stood here by group omitted most kinds the volumes emit (every store.* kind, dispatch.refused, seat.bundle.refused, every deploy.* and art.* kind, push.failed and more), so N-01 would have refused the factory's own records. test.proof is emitted by N-24 for dark builds (nodes/N-24/spec.xml#m-mirror).

Not record kinds: views (map.state, node.state, checklist.state, alert, health, hold.flag, counters and the others of nodes/N-31/spec.xml#views) are derived by the service and pushed by subscription; static kinds (node.spec, source.inventory, nodes/N-37/spec.xml#static-kinds) are generated into the map bundle at build. A panel binds one of the three (check.sh C20).

Line-op class (refused 403 from a seat): code.table, build-mode.state, rule.bit, cleanup.run, disposition, cancel, pr.close, branch.delete, promotion, exit.verdict, freeze.state, merge, verified, dispatch, job.run, ticket.request, lease.*, any flag. bin/make-kinds.py reads this statement for the class column, so this sentence is the one list.

store-table.name: plans
store-table.purpose: Suite and main plans with their Jenkins build numbers so a restart re-attaches to a running build; in-flight caps live in config (gate runs 2 with main first, image builds 2).
store-table.column: suite or main

store-table.name: suite_budget
store-table.purpose: Per suite: p95 of pod.run durations x 1.5, floor 5 min, cap 30 min, needs 20 samples; computed nightly.

store-rule.title: Owner-surface tables (G5)
store-rule.statement: cards(id, tier, source_record, dedupe_key, about, decide, options JSON, recommendation, default, deadline_at, status, version); rulings(card_id UNIQUE, pick, words, source, signal, at); messages(id, text, reply_to, at); acks(message_id, state, at, version); replies(message_id, text, at); routed_messages(message_id, lane, consumer, sla_seconds, at); watcher_alive(tier PRIMARY KEY, pid, heartbeat_at, version: the lock with heartbeat per tier); page_state(tier, version, rendered_seq, staleness, at); front_door(tier, bind, port, pid, at); plan_steps(plan_id, n, status, version); plan_sides(plan_id, n, status, version); ledger_rows(plan_id, seq, status, code, text, at); push_receipts(card_id, channel, delivered_at); cutover(page, state, imported_at, swapped_at, version).

store-rule.title: Governance tables (G7)
store-rule.statement: cleanup_runs(id, entry, plan_path, state, attempt, deleted JSON, remaining JSON, at); dispositions(entry_id, section, key, verdict, action, step, state, attempt, result_ref); publish_cursor(last_published_sha, version, at); promotions(tier, sha, attempt, state, pid, port, screenshot_id, previous_sha); exit_verdicts(day PRIMARY KEY, code, rows JSON, consecutive_fails); build_mode is the flags row.

store-rule.title: Map registries (G6)
store-rule.statement: bindings and machines are generated files in the repository (tools/map/registry/, N-37), not tables; their binding.record and binding.check rows are records; alerts are entities keyed by source record id with an alert.ack entity per acknowledgement.

store-table.name: counters
store-table.purpose: The counters view the Go service computes every tick for windows 1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 d and the previous window of each, keyed by window plus tick minute; single writer; a lower-at frame is dropped; never a second metrics database.
store-table.column: cut, started, tested, reviewed, merged
median and p95
store-table.rule: Every count is a count over record kinds in records, never a seat tally.

retention.s: Retention is a class per kind registered with N-45, and a retention run deletes rows: N-45 deletes the expired rows of a class and advances store:epoch min_retained_seq in the same Commit (contracts.xml#epoch-cursor), so a backup verifier and a Tail cursor know the floor. Classes: record (records kept for the life of the store; the backups are the archive), owner-surface (page.* other than page.state 90 days; messages and replies for the life of the store), plan (90 days), screen (pushed frames not stored, frame.report 7 days), lease (released, expired or revoked rows 30 days), forge (forge_history 30 days), health (health_history 30 days), effects (done or failed 30 days), heartbeat (7 days after seat.result). Entity-only kinds (page.state, ticks, health:service, heartbeats, watcher.alive) keep one current row each and no history in records.

Every state path under the store's root (STATE/store/coq.db, its WAL, STATE/backup/store/, STATE/run/service.lock, STATE/config/service.env) is an entry in shared/cleanup-registry.json with line/bin/cleanup.sh --entry ID as its verb; the live database file is never a cleanup target.

Free space: a Commit is refused 503 store.disk under store.min_free_mib, except the store.reserve_mib kept for health and restore records; a backup is skipped once under backup.min_free_mib; N-45 cleanup runs first and one card follows if still under (failure-cases.xml#disk-full).

config-keys.s: Keys live in STATE/config/service.env and the config table; service credentials are not keys and live with coq-svc (shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix); Scheduler.Reload applies a change without a restart; every value is a key, never a literal in code (K10); a missing key is exit 3 naming it. The timing and capacity keys below carry the defaults of contracts.xml#timing, the one table; a node volume cites the key.

Site placeholders: every ${SITE_*} value in the book (${SITE_VPS_ADDR}, ${SITE_CI_LAN_ADDR}, ${SITE_PI_LAN_ADDR}, ${SITE_TAILNET_HOST}, ${SITE_TAILNET_ADDR}, ${SITE_JENKINS_HOST}, ${SITE_K8S_WORKER}, ${SITE_K8S_ADMIN}) resolves from the owner's site file $HOME/.config/coq/site.env, mode 0600, never in the repository; ${HOME_SLUG} is the -home-USER- Claude project slug derived from $HOME. The service reads the site file at start and refuses to start (exit 3) when a key a live node needs is missing.
config-keys.config-key: one key read by N-02, N-07, N-12 and N-15; N-12's dead-launcher bound is 3 x this (90 s)
node:N-07:leader, renewed every 10 s

owner-tunable; meaning in shared/retry-budget.xml#budgets

config-key.default: tick 48h, daily 30d, monthly 12mo, manual until card

config-keys.config-key: N-45 applies it
the newest verified off-host copy is never older than this, else one card

many-agents.readers: Every node reads through N-01 (Store.Get, List, Tail, Snapshot); fifty readers at once are one SQLite WAL reader each; Tail fans out seq in order within one epoch to every consumer.
many-agents.writers: One process (coq-service, user coq-svc) holds the write lock; every write is one Store.Commit or Store.Do under an operation key (contracts.xml#batch); a seat never holds the file or the socket; a second service instance is refused by flock on STATE/run/service.lock (failure-cases.xml#duplicate-instance).
many-agents.collision: Two writers on one entity: the second compare-and-swap misses, 409 version; two grants on one lease key: the second fails its guard, 423 or 412 (contracts.xml#lease-machine); two commits under one operation key: the second replays 200 or, with a different request hash, 409 idempotency_mismatch; a stale or non-current token: 412; none of these waits and none overwrites.
many-agents.test: N-01 test (planned, not-run): 20 goroutines Commit under one operation key; exactly one row; 19 replays; the six effects of one run under six keys all commit. N-02 test (planned, not-run): 20 GrantDispatch on one ticket and phase; one lease; 19 refusals.
